reason: E3 directly supports laser cladding of WC-containing coatings on TC4 and resulting hardness/wear improvements, but it also notes increased brittleness, contradicting the premise that ductility is uncompromised. E2 supports WC reinforcement benefits but in a different HEA matrix, not TC4. E4 highlights TiAl brittleness, further challenging the ductility premise. E1 is irrelevant. Thus, key premises are only partly supported, with a major gap regarding ductility retention.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit a composite coating with well-dispersed WC particles on TC4.
WC particle reinforcement increases hardness and wear resistance in metallic matrices.
A TiAl-based intermetallic matrix can be formed during laser cladding on TC4.
The composite coating can improve surface properties without compromising the ductility of the underlying TC4.
